1.title: Two Letters, One Journey
1.context: This short letter traveled with the letter to the Colossians, carried by Tychicus and Onesimus (Colossians 4:7-9). Paul writes it from prison; the series places it with the other prison letters at Rome, a placement the letter itself does not name.
1.question: Who in your life receives your most personal letters, and what does that say about the trust between you?

1.title: A Sister, a Soldier, and a Church
1.context: The letter is addressed to a household: Philemon, Apphia, Archippus, and the church meeting in Philemon's house. House churches were the normal meeting places of the first believers.
1.question: What does it change that Paul's most personal request is addressed to a whole household and its church, not to one man alone?

1.title: Partnership in the Faith
1.context: Paul's thanksgiving names the reports that reached him: Philemon's faith toward the Lord Jesus and his love for all the saints. The partnership Paul prays about here is the word he will call on at the letter's climax.
1.question: Whose faith and love do you thank God for by name, and have you told them?

1.title: Refreshed Hearts
1.context: Refreshed is the letter's signature word: the hearts of the saints have been refreshed through Philemon, and Paul will ask the same refreshment for his own heart before the letter ends.
1.question: Who has refreshed your heart in a hard season, and whose heart might you refresh this week?

2.title: The Road Not Taken
2.context: Paul claims the right to command what is proper, then sets the right aside and appeals on the basis of love, presenting himself as an aged man and a prisoner of Christ Jesus.
2.question: When have you chosen to appeal rather than demand, and what did it cost or gain?

2.title: My Child Onesimus
2.context: Onesimus means useful in Greek, and Paul's wordplay turns on the name: formerly useless to Philemon, now useful to both. Paul says he became Onesimus's father in the faith while in chains.
2.question: Who became family to you in an unlikely place, the way Onesimus became Paul's child in a prison?

2.title: My Very Heart
2.context: Paul sends Onesimus back though he wanted to keep him as a helper in Philemon's place. The letter never says how Onesimus came to be with Paul; Paul's own word is that he was separated from Philemon for a while.
2.question: What have you had to send back or give up because it was not yours to keep?

2.title: Not Out of Compulsion
2.context: Paul refuses to act without Philemon's consent, so that the goodness would be voluntary rather than forced. The appeal protects the freedom of the man it asks the most of.
2.question: Where might you be pressuring someone into a good act that only counts if they choose it freely?

2.title: No Longer as a Slave
2.context: Paul frames the separation with a perhaps and a purpose: Philemon might have Onesimus back for good, no longer as a slave but as a beloved brother, in person and in the Lord.
2.question: What would it mean to receive someone back not in their old place, but as a brother or sister?

3.title: Receive Him as You Would Receive Me
3.context: Partner is the word from the letter's thanksgiving, now called in: if Philemon counts Paul a partner, Onesimus is to be received with the same welcome Paul himself would receive.
3.question: Who are you asked to welcome at a level that costs you standing or comfort?

3.title: Written with My Own Hand
3.context: Paul covers any debt Onesimus owes and signs the promise in his own hand, the ancient equivalent of a signature on a note, then mentions once, and only to dismiss it, that Philemon owes him his very self.
3.question: When has someone covered a cost for you that you could not repay, and how did it change the relationship?

3.title: Refresh My Heart
3.context: Refresh my heart answers the letter's opening: the hearts of the saints refreshed through Philemon are now joined by Paul's own. Paul writes confident Philemon will do even more than he asks, and leaves the more unnamed.
3.question: What is the unnamed more that love might be asking of you beyond the minimum?

3.title: A Guest Room and Greetings
3.context: Paul hopes to be released and to visit, and asks for a guest room in the same house Onesimus is returning to. The greetings name Epaphras, Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, the fellow workers around the prison letters.
3.question: How does expecting to meet face to face change the way you write, ask, or promise?
